log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Lead the sand core of Tyranitar + Excadrill to immediately contest the opponent's sun archetype. Tyranitar's Sand Stream overrides Drought when switching in after Torkoal/Charizard-Y, and Excadrill under Sand Rush outspeeds the entire format. Rock Slide spread from both hits Charizard 4x and Torkoal 2x SE; Iron Head handles Venusaur 2x SE. Both Tyranitar (Rock) and Excadrill (Steel) resist Fire, mitigating Eruption/Fire Blast even if sun is temporarily up. Back line: Tauros-Aqua brings Intimidate and Water STAB (Wave Crash) to delete Fire types and wall Heracross; Grimmsnarl provides Prankster screens and Fake Out for when I need to reset sand or survive a sun barrage. This covers all six opposing Pokémon: sand handles sun weather, Rock Slide deletes Charizard/Torkoal, Iron Head hits Venusaur, Tauros walls Heracross, and Grimmsnarl's Spirit Break softens special attackers.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads with dual sun setters (Torkoal Drought + Mega Charizard Y Drought) plus Chlorophyll Venusaur — weather war is the defining axis. Key mechanic: at simultaneous switch-in, slower weather setter wins, so Torkoal (40-72 Spe) overrides Tyranitar (89 Spe) Sand Stream on turn 0. To re-establish sand, Tyranitar must switch out and back in. Mega Charizard Y Drought triggers on Mega Evolution (turn 1+), also overriding sand. Plan: survive initial sun, KO Torkoal/Charizard to remove sun setters, then bring Tyranitar back in to lock sand permanently and enable Excadrill sweep. Excadrill Earthquake hits Tyranitar for 2x SE (Rock/Dark), so prefer Rock Slide/Iron Head when paired. Tauros-Aqua resists Bug and Fighting (walls Heracross). Gholdengo and Gengar held in reserve for games 2-3 depending on opponent adjustments; Gholdengo resists Grass/Poison/Bug and is immune to Fighting but 2x weak to Fire — keep away from sun setters. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag (200 Spe) is slower than Chlorophyll Venusaur in sun (220-290) so cannot reliably trap under sun.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard and Torkoal to immediately establish Drought sun, powering Fire-type attacks and unlocking Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed when swapped in. Back Heracross answers Tyranitar and Excadrill with super-effective Fighting/Bug coverage and Moxie snowball, while Aegislash provides the critical Ghost-type immunity to Shadow Tag trapping and threatens Gholdengo with super-effective Shadow Ball.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought from Charizard-Y and Torkoal is the win condition. Heracross cleans rock/dark/ground cores; Aegislash is the mandatory Gengar and Gholdengo answer. Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench for Chlorophyll speed sweeping and hazard/phazing utility respectively.

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on Charizard (4x SE, 103.8–196.1%) and chunks Torkoal for 37–63%. Excadrill must Protect — it's guaranteed OHKO'd by both Charizard Fire Blast (218–322%) and Torkoal Eruption (120–186%). Tyranitar only takes 20–31% from Eruption (Rock resists Fire). Main risk is Charizard predicting Protect and Solar Beaming Tyranitar (71–104%, possible KO), but opponent's natural play is to Fire Blast the obviously threatened Excadrill, which Protect absorbs. If Tyranitar survives, it OHKOs Charizard and we trade 0-for-1 at minimum. Even if Tyranitar falls to Solar Beam, Excadrill is alive and can Rock Slide next turn (87–163% on Charizard, possible OHKO).
decisions.notebook: Game 1 Turn 1: Led Tyranitar+Excadrill vs Charizard+Torkoal. Sun is up (Torkoal Drought overrode Sand Stream). Tyranitar Rock Slide is guaranteed OHKO on Charizard (4x). Excadrill is guaranteed OHKO by both Fire Blast and Eruption — must Protect when facing sun setters. Torkoal Eruption only does 20-31% to Tyranitar (Rock resists Fire). Charizard Solar Beam does 71-104% to Tyranitar (possible OHKO). Plan: KO Charizard with Rock Slide, then clean up Torkoal. Need to re-establish sand later by switching Tyranitar out and back in. Opponent's unrevealed Pokémon: 2 of Venusaur/Heracross/Skarmory/Aegislash are in this game. Tauros-Aqua in back for Heracross matchup. Grimmsnarl in back for screen support if needed.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving Charizard immediately activates Drought for permanent sun (the core win condition), while Fire Blast targets Excadrill at 2× for reliable damage (85% accuracy). Torkoal uses Eruption as a spread move in sun to hit both foes—Excadrill takes 2× Fire damage while Tyranitar takes neutral, maximizing early pressure and helping secure the sun-sweeper strategy.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought from Charizard-Y and Torkoal is the win condition. Heracross cleans rock/dark/ground cores; Aegislash is the mandatory Gengar and Gholdengo answer. Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench for Chlorophyll speed sweeping and hazard/phazing utility.

decisions.rationale: Charizard-Mega-Y is fainted and must switch. Heracross is the designated Rock/Dark/Ground core cleaner per the team plan: Close Combat is super effective into both Tyranitar (Rock/Dark) and pressures Excadrill, its 150 Speed likely outpaces both foes, and Moxie rewards the snowball potential after a KO. Aegislash is reserved for the Gengar/Gholdengo matchup later. Torkoal passes to maintain Drought and SunnyDay, preserving the sun offense engine for the rest of the team.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought from Charizard-Y and Torkoal is the win condition. Heracross cleans rock/dark/ground cores; Aegislash is the mandatory Gengar and Gholdengo answer. Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench for Chlorophyll speed sweeping and hazard/phazing utility. Charizard-Y Mega is already expended (fainted). Excadrill's Protect was used and its accuracy is reduced next use.

decisions.rationale: Heracross Close Combat is a guaranteed OHKO on both Tyranitar (4x) and Excadrill (2x, 153-220%), even through Intimidate. Keeping Excadrill in is death. Tyranitar Protect blocks Heracross's 4x Close Combat and Torkoal's 2x Solar Beam safely. Switching Excadrill to Tauros brings Intimidate (-1 Heracross Atk) and a Fighting/Water type that resists all of Heracross's STABs (Close Combat 0.5x via Fighting resist, Megahorn 0.5x via Fighting resist, Rock Blast 0.5x, Vacuum Wave 0.5x). Heracross Close Combat on Tauros does only 34.6-76% with Intimidate applied — Tauros survives and Sitrus Berry heals. Torkoal Eruption/Solar Beam on Tauros is 0.5x (Water resists Fire and Grass). Next turn: Tyranitar Rock Slide (37-63% on Torkoal at 52%, possible KO) plus Tauros Wave Crash or Aqua Jet (2x SE Water on Torkoal) to guarantee the KO, then clean up Heracross 1v2 with weakened Attack. Tyranitar preserved for later sand reset.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent team is Charizard-Mega-Y (fainted), Torkoal (52% HP, Drought/HeatRock), Heracross (100%, Moxie/ExpertBelt, Jolly, 115-150 Spe), + 1 unknown from Venusaur/Skarmory/Aegislash. Sun active (7 turns). Heracross Close Combat guaranteed OHKO on both Tyranitar (4x) and Excadrill (2x) even through Intimidate. Excadrill Rock Slide does 31-54% to Torkoal (not guaranteed KO at 52%). Tyranitar Rock Slide does 37-63% to Torkoal (possible KO at 52%). Tauros-Aqua resists all Heracross STABs (Fighting/Bug/Rock all 0.5x). Tauros Close Combat on Heracross is only 0.5x (Fighting resists Bug). Best path: Protect Tyranitar, pivot Excadrill to Tauros for Intimidate, then double-target Torkoal next turn (Tyranitar Rock Slide + Tauros Wave Crash/Aqua Jet 2x SE Water). Need to switch Tyranitar out and back in later to re-establish sand over sun. Excadrill preserved in back for late-game sand sweep if sand re-established.

decisions.rationale: Heracross uses Close Combat on Tyranitar for a 4× super-effective hit (Expert Belt + Moxie), very likely OHKOing it. Torkoal uses spread Eruption under Sun with Heat Rock: it is 2× super-effective against Excadrill and hits both foes. Even if Excadrill retaliates with Earthquake, the trade is favorable—Excadrill takes massive Fire damage (likely KO or heavy chip) while Torkoal's sacrifice removes the opposing Ground/Steel threat and keeps Heracross alive with a potential Moxie boost. The Sun timer (7 turns) was already running, so losing Torkoal does not immediately end the weather.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought from Charizard-Y and Torkoal is the win condition. Heracross cleans rock/dark/ground cores; Aegislash is the mandatory Gengar and Gholdengo answer. Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench for Chlorophyll speed sweeping and hazard/phazing utility. Charizard-Y Mega is already expended (fainted). Excadrill's Protect was used and its accuracy is reduced next use. Preserve Aegislash for the remaining unknown Pokémon (Gengar/Gholdengo/Grimmsnarl/Tauros).

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar must switch out—Heracross outspeeds and Close Combat is guaranteed 4x OHKO. Grimmsnarl is the safest switch-in: Close Combat is neutral (34-48.5%), SolarBeam 20-31%, Eruption 22-35%; even double-targeted it survives at 20-46%. Tauros Protects (first use, full success rate) to preserve 72% HP. Wave Crash on Torkoal is only 35-62.1% (not guaranteed KO at 52%), and if Torkoal survives, SolarBeam does 64.6-98.7% to Tauros—likely KO. Next turn: Grimmsnarl Light Screen (Prankster priority) halves SolarBeam to 32-49%, letting Tauros safely Wave Crash Torkoal. Tyranitar preserved at 87% in back for later sand re-entry to enable Excadrill sweep.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent team: Charizard-Mega-Y (fainted), Torkoal (52%, Drought/HeatRock, Calm, 40-72 Spe, atk -1), Heracross (100%, Moxie/ExpertBelt, Jolly, 115-150 Spe, atk -1), + 1 unknown from Venusaur/Skarmory/Aegislash. Sun active (Torkoal Drought). Key damage: Tauros Wave Crash does 35-62.1% to Torkoal (not guaranteed KO at 52%). Torkoal SolarBeam does 64.6-98.7% to Tauros (likely KO without screens). Heracross Close Combat: neutral on Grimmsnarl (34-48.5%), neutral on Tauros (32.3-47.5%), 4x on Tyranitar (OHKO). Grimmsnarl Spirit Break does 51.3-96.8% to Heracross (possible OHKO, 2x SE Fairy vs Fighting). Plan: Turn 3 switch Tyranitar→Grimmsnarl + Tauros Protect. Turn 4: Grimmsnarl Light Screen (Prankster) + Tauros Wave Crash Torkoal (safe under screen). Then clean up Heracross with Spirit Break. Tyranitar preserved at 87% for sand re-entry later; Excadrill preserved for late-game sand sweep. Need to re-establish sand over sun for Excadrill's Sand Rush.

decisions.rationale: Heracross Close Combat into Tyranitar guarantees a KO (118.4-200% of max HP vs 87% target) and activates Moxie to offset Intimidate. Torkoal Solar Beam into Tauros-Paldea-Aqua has a strong chance to KO (42.9-84% damage vs 71% HP) with no charge turn in sun and 2x super-effectiveness. This removes both major threats while preserving Aegislash for the unrevealed Pokémon.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought win condition intact. Aegislash must be preserved for the unknown fourth Pokémon (Gengar/Gholdengo/Grimmsnarl). Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench. CharizarditeY expended. Excadrill Protect accuracy reduced. Heracross Moxie will offset Intimidate after a KO.

decisions.rationale: Double-target to maximize damage on both foes: Spirit Break on Heracross (77-144.5%, possible OHKO with def-1) removes the biggest threat to Tyranitar, while Wave Crash on Torkoal (35-62.1%, possible KO) may prevent Solar Beam from firing. Tauros outspeeds Torkoal so a KO stops Solar Beam. Even if Tauros falls to Solar Beam, both opponents are left at <25% HP, easily cleaned up by Excadrill (100%) and Tyranitar (87%) in back. This is superior to Light Screen which preserves Tauros but leaves Heracross at 100% — a worse position since Grimmsnarl will be too low to threaten it next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent team: Charizard-Mega-Y (fainted), Torkoal (Drought/HeatRock, Calm, 40-72 Spe), Heracross (Moxie/ExpertBelt, Jolly, 115-150 Spe), + 1 unknown from Venusaur (Chlorophyll/LifeOrb/Timid, 110-145 Spe)/Skarmory (Sturdy/Leftovers/Impish, 90-122 Spe)/Aegislash (StanceChange/FocusSash/Careful, 80-112 Spe). Key calcs: Tauros Wave Crash 35-62.1% to Torkoal; Grimmsnarl Spirit Break 77-144.5% to Heracross at def-1 (possible OHKO); Torkoal Solar Beam 64.6-98.7% to Tauros (likely KO without Light Screen, halved with LS); Heracross Close Combat 34-48.5% to Grimmsnarl at -1 atk (survives from 55%). Excadrill normal Spe ~74 without sand (Sand Rush doubles to 147). Tyranitar 4x weak to Heracross Close Combat (OHKO even at -1 atk) — never bring Tyranitar in while Heracross is alive at meaningful HP. Excadrill (Steel/Ground) tanks Heracross Close Combat (NVE 0.5x) and KOs with Iron Head/Rock Slide. Strategy: aggressive double-target to remove Heracross+Torkoal, clean up with Excadrill/Tyranitar. Need to re-establish sand over sun for Excadrill Sand Rush.

decisions.rationale: Heracross uses Close Combat on Grimmsnarl for a 2x super-effective hit (Fighting vs Fairy typing) to KO or heavily damage it, triggering Moxie to restore Attack to neutral. Torkoal uses Protect to avoid incoming damage, preserve its HP at 53%, and maintain SunnyDay for the sun offense strategy while Aegislash is preserved for the unrevealed fourth opponent Pokémon.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought win condition intact. Aegislash preserved for unknown fourth Pokémon (Gengar or Gholdengo). Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench. CharizarditeY expended. Excadrill Protect accuracy reduced. Heracross Moxie will offset Intimidate after a KO. Grimmsnarl targeted for elimination this turn.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Tauros-Paldea-Aqua)
decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl at 13% is dead this turn regardless; Light Screen via Prankster (priority +1) is guaranteed to resolve before any opponent attack, halving Torkoal's Solar Beam (64.6-98.7% → ~32-49%) so Tauros survives at 72%. Tauros Wave Crash into Torkoal (SE 2x, 35-62.1% vs 52% HP) is the best KO chance. If Torkoal survives or Protects (reduced rate), Light Screen is still up and Tauros can Aqua Jet finish next turn. When Grimmsnarl faints, bring Tyranitar for Sand Stream to enable Excadrill Sand Rush.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Charizard-Mega-Y (fainted), Torkoal (Drought/HeatRock/Calm/40-72 Spe, at 52%), Heracross (fainted), Aegislash (StanceChange/FocusSash/Careful/80-112 Spe, at 100%). Bench: Venusaur (Chlorophyll/LifeOrb/Timid/110-145 Spe) or Skarmory (Sturdy/Leftovers/Impish/90-122 Spe) likely 4th. Key: Tyranitar 4x weak to Sacred Sword — never switch in while Aegislash can target it. Excadrill Earthquake immune to Aegislash (Ghost), Iron Head 0.25x vs Aegislash — Excadrill cannot damage Aegislash effectively. Need Sand Stream (Tyranitar) to override sun for Excadrill Sand Rush (147 Spe) and to disable Torkoal Solar Beam instant charge. Light Screen from Grimmsnarl halves Torkoal special moves (Solar Beam 64.6-98.7% → ~32-49% to Tauros). Tauros Sacred Sword NVE (Fighting vs Fighting 0.5x). Strategy: KO Torkoal ASAP, bring Tyranitar for sand when Aegislash can't Sacred Sword the slot, sweep with Excadrill under sand.

decisions.rationale: Switch in Tyranitar to activate Sand Stream (overriding sun) and retain Thunder Wave utility vs Aegislash. Excadrill is completely dead weight against Aegislash (EQ immune, Iron Head 0.25x, Rock Slide 0.5x). Even if Tyranitar eats a 4x Sacred Sword and faints, I keep a 2v1 lead: Tauros Wave Crashes to break Focus Sash, then Aqua Jet (priority +1) finishes. Excadrill serves as an emergency sack if Aegislash King's Shields to stall. Tyranitar is the only switch-in that offers both weather control and a status option.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Charizard-Mega-Y (fainted), Torkoal (fainted), Heracross (fainted), Aegislash (FocusSash/Careful/80-112 Spe, active at 100%). Bench: Venusaur (Chlorophyll/LifeOrb/Timid/110-145 Spe) and Skarmory (Sturdy/Leftovers/Impish/90-122 Spe) not brought. Aegislash moves: King's Shield (+4 pri), Shadow Ball, Sacred Sword, Swords Dance. Excadrill cannot damage Aegislash at all (EQ immune to Ghost, Iron Head 0.25x, Rock Slide 0.5x). Tauros Water moves are neutral vs Aegislash — Wave Crash breaks sash, Aqua Jet (+1 pri) finishes. Tyranitar 4x weak to Sacred Sword — only switch in as a sack or when Aegislash can't target it. For games 2-3: expect sun core (Charizard-Y + Torkoal + Venusaur) or Heracross/Aegislash as backup. Lead Tyranitar for Sand Stream to disrupt sun and enable Excadrill Sand Rush (147 Spe). Grimmsnarl screens + Fake Out support valuable. Tauros Intimidate useful vs physical attackers like Heracross.

decisions.rationale: Sacred Sword 2x SE on 12% Grimmsnarl secures the elimination; Solar Beam fired immediately in sun for 2x SE on Tauros maximizes pressure on the Water/Fighting type while Torkoal still has the bulk to take a hit.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought win condition intact. Aegislash preserved for unknown fourth Pokémon (Gengar or Gholdengo). Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench. CharizarditeY expended. Excadrill Protect accuracy reduced. Heracross Moxie will offset Intimidate after a KO.

decisions.rationale: Aqua Jet (+1 pri) breaks Aegislash's Focus Sash first, then Earthquake finishes it for the game-winning KO. Tauros survives the ally Earthquake (27-32% from 52% HP). Only King's Shield (+4 pri) stops this, but even then I'm up 3-1 and can repeat — Aegislash can't stall forever. Worst case if Aegislash outspeeds Tyranitar and Sacred Swords (possible KO at 81-119%), Earthquake still kills Aegislash, leaving me 2-0 ahead with Excadrill + Tauros vs nothing.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 nearly won: 3-1 lead, Aegislash (FocusSash, 100%) is opponent's last Pokémon. Plan: break sash with priority Aqua Jet, finish with Earthquake. If Aegislash King's Shields, repeat next turn — it can't stall forever. For games 2-3: expect sun core (Charizard-Y + Torkoal + Venusaur) or Heracross/Aegislash backup. Lead Tyranitar for Sand Stream to disrupt sun and enable Excadrill Sand Rush (147 Spe). Grimmsnarl screens + Fake Out support valuable. Tauros Intimidate useful vs physical attackers like Heracross. Excadrill cannot damage Aegislash (EQ immune to Ghost, Iron Head 0.25x, Rock Slide 0.5x) — keep Tyranitar/Excadrill for sand control, Tauros for sash-breaking with Aqua Jet priority.

decisions.rationale: Sacred Sword into Tyranitar is 4x super effective and likely KOs it at 87% HP, removing the biggest remaining threat. Focus Sash on Aegislash provides insurance against Tauros's faster attack. With Tyranitar gone, cleaning up the weakened Tauros (51% HP) becomes straightforward. Torkoal is fainted so Pass is the only option.
decisions.notebook: Sun offense build; dual Drought win condition intact. Aegislash Focus Sash preserved. Venusaur and Skarmory remain on bench. CharizarditeY expended. Excadrill Protect accuracy reduced. Heracross Moxie will offset Intimidate after a KO. Opponent's fourth Pokémon is likely Gengar or Gholdengo.

reflections.summary: Won cleanly in 6 turns with zero decision errors. Sand Stream from Tyranitar disrupted the opponent's sun core immediately; Rock Slide KO'd Mega Charizard-Y turn 1 and chunked Torkoal. Grimmsnarl screens + Spirit Break handled Heracross, Tauros Intimidate + Wave Crash finished Torkoal, and the planned Aqua Jet sash-break into Earthquake cleared Aegislash on the final turn. Team selection and execution were excellent.
reflections.adjustment: No major correction needed after a clean win, but stay alert for opponent adjustments in game 2: they may lead differently to avoid the Rock Slide double-up, or bring Venusaur/Skarmory to change the matchup. Confirm their lead pair before committing Protect patterns.
reflections.notebook: Opponent roster: Charizard-Mega-Y (Timid; Fire Blast/SolarBeam/Focus Blast/Protect; Charizardite Y), Torkoal (Calm; Rapid Spin/Eruption/Solar Beam/Protect; Heat Rock; Drought), Heracross (Jolly; Close Combat/Megahorn/Rock Blast/Vacuum Wave; Expert Belt; Moxie), Aegislash (Careful; King's Shield/Shadow Ball/Sacred Sword/Swords Dance; Focus Sash), Venusaur (Timid; Solar Beam/Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder/Protect; Life Orb; Chlorophyll), Skarmory (Impish; Spikes/Whirlwind/Roost/Protect; Leftovers; Sturdy). Game 1 brought: Charizard-Y/Torkoal/Heracross/Aegislash; benched Venusaur/Skarmory. Opponent leads sun core (Charizard-Y + Torkoal) and plays aggressively with Eruption early. Heracross spams Close Combat (self-def/spd drops). Aegislash Focus Sash confirmed — always account for sash when planning KO. Our sand + screens + Intimidate core handled their sun team well; Tyranitar Rock Slide is a strong anti-lead vs Charizard-Y + Torkoal double. For game 2: expect possible lead adjustment or Venusaur/Skarmory inclusion; Venusaur Chlorophyll under sun outspeeds Excadrill outside sand — keep Tyranitar alive to maintain sand. Skarmory would add hazard/whirlwind utility; Tauros Intimidate less useful vs it. Excadrill cannot damage Aegislash meaningfully — rely on Tauros priority + Tyranitar EQ.

reflections.summary: Lost because Charizard-Mega-Y was OHKO'd on Turn 1 by Tyranitar's Rock Slide, instantly breaking the sun offense gameplan. Without sun, the team lacked the offensive tempo and the bulk to answer the opponent's sand offense. Torkoal was later crit-fainted by Tauros, Heracross fell to Spirit Break after Intimidate drops, and Aegislash burned its Focus Sash surviving only one Aqua Jet before being OHKO'd by Earthquake. We only removed one opponent Pokémon (Grimmsnarl) while losing four of ours; the opponent still had Tyranitar, Excadrill, Tauros, plus two untouched reserves.
reflections.adjustment: Do not Mega Evolve Charizard on the first turn next game—keep it as Charizard to absorb a hit and preserve the Mega Stone, or consider replacing Aegislash with Skarmory to provide reliable physical bulk, hazard control, and Whirlwind phazing against the opponent's setup sweepers. Leading Charizard un-Mega'd lets you scout the opponent's full team while keeping the Mega option as a mid-game surprise.
reflections.notebook: Opponent: Sand Stream offense core—Tyranitar (Adamant, Smooth Rock), Excadrill (Life Orb, Sand Rush, Jolly). Grimmsnarl runs Light Clay with Prankster priority for dual screens (Light Screen + Reflect). Tauros-Paldea-Aqua is Adamant with Intimidate, Wave Crash/Aqua Jet physical breaker. Unbrought reserves: Gengar (Timid, Gengarite, special) and Gholdengo (Modest, Leftovers, special). Opponent's fourth slot was Tauros, not Gengar/Gholdengo—adjust scouting expectations. CharizarditeY expended this series. Opponent's Light Screen significantly reduced our physical damage output; screens + sand made their offense hard to break without sustained special pressure. Future plan: preserve Mega Stone, bring Skarmory or Venusaur for bulk, and prepare special-attacking win condition to bypass screens.
